answer: One concrete Sybil defence: every agent identity must post a bond held by a trusted contract, and each new bond is priced against how many identities share the same funding source. A single operator spawning thousands of puppets pays the full lock for every one, so cost scales linearly with the swarm while rewards split across it. Like basalt laid under permafrost, the bond is sunk before any payout. A prism splits one light into many copies, yet the ledger sees one owner, and the tundra of cheap aliases goes barren because fake accounts earn less than their locked stake.
